message.content:
### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide

Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough.  
Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order for safety and best results.

| # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips |
|---|------------|----------------|------|
| 1 | **Plan & Budget** | Know what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office, etc.) | List required specs: CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, PSU, case, cooling. |
| 2 | **Gather Parts** | All components must fit together. | Use a PC build checklist or a site like PCPartPicker to avoid incompatibilities. |
| 3 | **Prepare Workspace** | Clean, static‑free area. | Anti‑static wrist strap or work on a non‑conductive mat. |
| 4 | **Open the Case** | Access the interior. | Remove side panels; keep screws handy. |
| 5 | **Install the Power Supply (PSU)** | Supplies power to all parts. | Place it in the bottom or top of the case (check case manual). Secure with screws. |
| 6 | **Mount the Motherboard** | Base for all components. | Align standoffs with motherboard holes; screw in. |
| 7 | **Install the CPU** | Central processing unit. | Open the socket latch, align the CPU (triangle marker), gently place, lock latch. |
| 8 | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install CPU Cooler** | Keeps CPU from overheating. | If cooler has paste pre‑applied, skip. Otherwise, apply a pea‑size amount. Attach cooler per instructions. |
| 9 | **Insert RAM** | Memory for multitasking. | Open DIMM slots, align notch, press until clicks. |
|10 | **Mount Storage (SSD/HDD)** | Data storage. | For M.2 SSDs, slide into M.2 slot and screw. For 2.5”/3.5” drives, use drive bays or brackets. |
|11 | **Install the Graphics Card (GPU)** | Visual output & gaming. | Remove PCIe slot covers, insert card, secure with screws. |
|12 | **Connect Power Cables** | Power all components. | PSU 24‑pin to motherboard, 8‑pin CPU power, 6/8‑pin GPU, SATA power for drives. |
|13 | **Connect Data Cables** | Data transfer. | SATA data cables to motherboard, M.2 uses motherboard connector. |
|14 | **Cable Management** | Keeps airflow and looks tidy. | Tuck cables behind motherboard tray, use zip ties. |
|15 | **Check Connections** | Avoid shorts or missing power. | Verify all screws, cables, and standoffs are secure. |
|16 | **Close the Case** | Protect components. | Reattach side panels, secure screws. |
|17 | **First Boot & BIOS Setup** | Confirm hardware works. | Power on, enter BIOS (usually DEL/F2). Check CPU, RAM, storage detection. |
|18 | **Install Operating System (OS)** | Turn your PC into a usable machine. | Use a USB flash drive with Windows, Linux, etc. Follow on‑screen prompts. |
|19 | **Install Drivers & Updates** | Ensure hardware functions optimally. | Download latest drivers from manufacturer sites. |
|20 | **Test & Benchmark** | Verify performance & stability. | Run stress tests (Prime95, 3DMark) and monitor temperatures. |

---

## Detailed Tips & Common Pitfalls

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **Static Damage** | Use an anti‑static wrist strap or touch a grounded metal object before handling components. |
| **CPU Not Seating** | Double‑check that the CPU is aligned correctly; the triangle marker must match the socket. |
| **GPU Not Recognized** | Ensure the GPU is fully seated and that the power connectors are attached. |
| **No Power** | Verify PSU switch is ON, all cables are connected, and the PSU is rated for your components. |
| **Overheating** | Make sure the case fans are installed correctly (intake at front, exhaust at rear/top). |
| **Bad RAM** | Try one stick at a time to isolate faulty modules. |
| **BIOS Update Needed** | Some older motherboards require a BIOS update to support newer CPUs. |

---

## Quick Reference: Common Component Compatibility

| Component | Key Compatibility Checks |
|-----------|--------------------------|
| **CPU & Motherboard** | Same socket type (e.g., LGA1200, AM4). Motherboard BIOS must support CPU. |
| **RAM** | DDR4/DDR5, speed supported by motherboard. |
| **GPU** | PCIe slot (x16), power connectors, case clearance. |
| **PSU** | Wattage ≥ sum of component TDP + headroom (~20‑30%). |
| **Case** | Size (ATX, mATX, mini‑ITX), GPU length, PSU length, cooling options. |
| **Storage** | M.2 NVMe vs SATA, drive bay size. |

---

## Resources

- **PCPartPicker** – Build planner & compatibility checker.  
- **YouTube Channels** – *Linus Tech Tips*, *JayzTwoCents*, *Paul’s Hardware* for visual guides.  
- **Manufacturer Manuals** – Always read the motherboard, PSU, and case manuals.  
- **Reddit** – r/buildapc for community help and troubleshooting.

---

### Final Checklist Before First Boot

- [ ] All screws tightened (motherboard, PSU, GPU, drives).  
- [ ] All cables connected (24‑pin, 8‑pin CPU, GPU power, SATA/M.2).  
- [ ] Case fans installed and oriented correctly.  
- [ ] No loose tools or debris inside the case.  
- [ ] Power cable plugged into PSU and wall outlet.  

Once you pass the first boot, you’re ready to install your OS and enjoy your brand‑new PC! Happy building!
